Euſebius Ceſarienſis. ( Ii 5. Demonſt. Euang. c 3. IEuen as he who was Prieſt
of Nations was nener ſene to offer coi poral ſacrifices, but only bread & wine,

that come from him, exerciſing the ſpiritual office of Prieſthood in al nations
after the Eccleſiaſtical ordinances, do repreſent the myſteries of his bodie,
and healthful bloud in bread & wine. which myſteries Melchiſedech knew ſo

Geneſis, and you ſhal ſind Melchiſedech king of Salem, prince of this citie,
who euen then in figure of Chriſt offered bread and wine, and dedicated the
Chriſtian myſlerie in our Sauiours bod :e ind bloud. Idem Epiſt. ad Euagrium:
Melchiſedech offered not bloudie victims, but dedicated the Sacrament of
Chriſt in bread and wine, ſimple and pure ſacrifice. Idem. Queſt. in Gen. c.
: Our myſtetie is ſignified in the word of order, not by Aaron in imolat:ng
brute victims, but in offering bread and wine, that is the bodie and bloud of
our Lord Ieſus. Idem in e. 26. Matthei : Melchiſedech the Prieſt of God moſt
hiegh, by offering bread and wine, prefigured the Myſterie of the Euchariſt.
S. Chriſoſtom ( ho. 15 in Gen. ) Seeing the figure, thinck alſo I pray thee, of
the veririe ho.  After that Melchiſedee king of Salem brought bread and
wine ( for he was Prieſt of God moſt hiegh) Abraham receiued his oblations.
S.Auguſtin ( Epiſt. 95.) Melchiſedech bringing forth the ſacrament (or
myſtenie) of our Lords table, knew how to figurate his eternal pueſthood.
